title: A drought-fitted loss above a fixed dry-flow threshold raised runoff prediction error across 174 south-east Australian catchments
abstract: We test loss rules fitted during the Millennium Drought (1997-2009) against annual runoff in 2010-2021 at 174 south-east Australian catchments. Reference curves use 1951-1996 flow, current and prior rain, and temperature. A one-parameter loss above a fixed reference dry-flow threshold had 11-18% higher test mean squared error than proportional loss in both AGCD and SILO rain and linear and quadratic reference curves. All four marginal full-refit 95% block and spatial intervals for this penalty were above zero. Constant and proportional loss had no clear error ranking. Proportional loss lowered point error by 23-43% versus unchanged flow, but its full-refit gain was clear in only one of four variants. Thus this specific threshold did not improve transfer, and the data did not select a stable constant-versus-proportional rule. This reuses earlier observations and is not a blind new-data test. One drought, 12 test years, shared rain sources, marginal intervals without multiplicity correction, and baseline error limit inference. It does not identify a physical cause. Exact compatible inputs, code, predictions, bootstrap draws, audits and figures are supplied.
